title: RRC coverage flips in both directions across chains, so the flag tracks review batches rather than protocol or chain
content:
The per-chain coverage verdicts in this chunk contradict each other in both directions. Base Fluid sUSDS reads "**`Covered`**" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.2.2.1.1) and Arbitrum Fluid likewise (.3.1.1.1), while the Ethereum Fluid instance reads `Pending`. Base Aave USDC reads "**`Pending`**" (.2.3.1.1) and Arbitrum Aave USDC the same (.3.2.1.1), while the Ethereum Aave instances read `Covered` — as does Avalanche Aave v3 USDC (.4.1.1.1). Base Morpho Blue is `Covered` where all three Ethereum Morpho instances are `Pending`.

So coverage is not a property of the protocol: Aave is both Covered and Pending, Fluid is both, Morpho is both. Nor is it a property of the chain: Base holds Covered and Pending instances side by side, and so does Ethereum.

The most plausible remaining explanation is that the flag records whether *this document* has been through review, and that reviews are done in batches — a chain rollout here, a protocol family there — rather than by any systematic sweep of the venue set.

That reading is more useful than the alternative and also more deflating. It means a `Covered` flag says a review happened, not that the venue type is understood, and a `Pending` flag says no one has got to this document yet, not that the venue is riskier. Any attempt to reason about Spark's risk-review completeness by protocol or by chain will produce a coherent-looking answer that is not supported by how the flag is actually being applied.
description: Fluid is Pending on Ethereum but Covered on Base and Arbitrum, while Aave is Covered on Ethereum and Avalanche but Pending on Base and Arbitrum — neither dimension predicts the verdict.
